Anything not `anthropic` or `google` is treated as OpenAI-compatible. Adding an OpenAI-compatible provider is one `ProviderDefinition` entry.

## ProviderModelAdapter

```rust
let adapter = ProviderModelAdapter::new(ProviderAdapterConfig {
    providers: BTreeMap::from([("anthropic".into(), ProviderCredential { api_key, base_url })]),
    key_source: None,
});
```

- Implements `ModelAdapter`. `generate` returns one response; `stream` forwards text deltas and provider-reported usage as `ModelStreamFrame`s and ends with a `Final` frame.
- The default HTTP client has a 15-second connect timeout and a 300-second whole-request timeout (including streamed bodies). `with_client` accepts an injected client that keeps its own policy.
- A streamed request that gets a 429 or 5xx answer is retried **once**; a second failure is reported with an `After one retry:` prefix. Setting `settings.max_retries = 0` on the agent disables the retry. Errors carry `(retry after Ns)` when the response had a `retry-after` or rate-limit reset header.
- `stream_options.include_usage` is sent to OpenAI and DeepSeek only at their default base URL, and always to vLLM and Ollama. At OpenAI's default endpoint `max_tokens` becomes `max_completion_tokens`, and `temperature` is omitted for reasoning models (`o1*`, `o3*`, `o4*`, `gpt-5*` except `-chat`).
- Keys come from `ProviderCredential.api_key`, or from a `KeySource` when set (see below). A missing key returns a message naming the environment variable.
- Image attachments are only sent to models for which `model_supports_images(provider, model)` is true; other models get a text reference. See [Runs and Sessions](/hosts/rust-daemon/runs/) for the daemon's attachment limits.

### KeySource

```rust
pub trait KeySource: Send + Sync {
    fn pick(&self, provider: &str) -> Option<(String, String)>;           // (key id, key)
    fn report(&self, provider: &str, key_id: &str, failure: Option<&ModelFailure>);
    fn holds_keys(&self, provider: &str) -> bool { false }
    fn pick_untried(&self, provider: &str, tried: &[String]) -> Option<(String, String)>;
    fn resting(&self, provider: &str) -> Option<KeysResting>;
}
```

The adapter asks for a key per attempt and reports the outcome. A failure that blames the key (`classify_model_error`: rate limit, billing, auth) makes it pick another key within the same call. When every key rests, it returns an error that names the cause and when a key is ready again. The daemon's pool (`provider_keys`) implements this trait with strategies `fill_first`, `round_robin`, `random`, `least_used`.

## ChatGPT Subscription

`ChatGptResponsesAdapter::new(access_token, account_id)` talks to the ChatGPT backend Responses endpoint (`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`) with redirects disabled and the same bounded timeouts. It never falls back to API billing. OAuth storage, refresh and account selection belong to the host (`hosts/rust-daemon/src/chatgpt_auth*`). `ChatGptModelsAdapter` fetches the account's model catalog metadata. The daemon routes the provider id `chatgpt` to it.

## Pricing and Model Table

`models.rs` is a static table (`PRICING_TABLE_DATE`, currently `2026-09-23`) of `ModelInfo` rows: provider, lowercase model-id prefix (the longest match wins), `context_window`, `max_output`, `vision` and `ModelPricing` in micro-USD per million tokens (input, output, optional cached input). Helpers: `model_table()`, `model_info(provider, model)`, `price_usage`, `estimate_cost_micros` (returns `Priced`, `Free` for `ollama` and `vllm`, `Subscription`, or `Unknown`) and `canonical_provider_id`. The daemon uses it for context budgets (60% of the window, capped at 200,000 tokens) and usage pricing, with owner overrides layered on top.

## Speech and Transcription

`OpenAiTranscriptionAdapter` (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`) and `OpenAiSpeechAdapter` (`/v1/audio/speech`) implement the `TranscriptionPort` and `SpeechPort` contracts from `anima-service-adapters`. Both bound the number of outgoing bodies, honor a `CancelSignal` and use an OpenAI Platform API key only. The daemon enables them with `ANIMAOS_STT_ENABLED` and `ANIMAOS_TTS_ENABLED`.

## DeterministicModelAdapter

A fixed-text adapter (provider id `deterministic`) for tests and demos. The daemon has a separate in-process deterministic adapter used by its test and embedding constructors; the real daemon never uses either unless an agent selects the `deterministic` / `test` provider.

## Adding a Provider

1. OpenAI-compatible endpoint: add a `ProviderDefinition` to `PROVIDERS` in `catalog.rs`, with its environment variable names and a default base URL; add a pricing row in `models.rs` if you want cost and context data. Add a catalog test in `src/tests.rs`.
2. Different wire format: add an `Anthropic`-style kind in `provider_kind`, a body builder and parser module, and a stream consumer in `stream.rs`.
3. Host side: nothing else is needed for routing; the daemon builds its provider config from `provider_definitions()`. Credential storage, rotation and fallbacks are daemon concerns. For key pools and fallbacks see [Persistence](/hosts/rust-daemon/persistence/).

Hermes provider-format reuse is credited in `HERMES-NOTICE` in the crate directory.

Tests are mock-server based (`axum` dev-dependency); no real provider is called. Run `cargo test -p anima-model-adapters`.
anima-service-adapters, anima-document-content, anima-process, anima-acp and anima-worktree

Five crates support the daemon's tools. They are reusable libraries, kept in `packages/core-rust` so another host could use them. None implements HTTP routes or owns agent policy; the daemon decides authority, approvals and persistence.

| Crate | Depends on | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| `anima-service-adapters` | `anima-core` | Passive contracts and validation: browser, connectors, community bundles, speech and transcription, documents, token-cost estimation |
| `anima-document-content` | `anima-service-adapters` | DOCX, PDF and XLSX text extraction from bytes |
| `anima-process` | none | Process custody, PTY app sessions |
| `anima-acp` | `anima-process` | Agent Client Protocol client |
| `anima-worktree` | none | Git worktree isolation for helper agents |

## anima-service-adapters

"This crate depends on the engine; the engine never depends on this crate." It defines data, bounds and traits; hosts implement transports and enforce authority.

| Module | Contents |
|--------|----------|
| `browser` | `BrowserScope`, `BrowserOperation`, `BrowserObservation`, `BrowserPort` and strict, bounded decoders and digests (for example 16 routes, 40 actions, 80 requests, 120 s per scope, 128 observation nodes). A scope is admission data, not an owner grant; the crate launches no browser. |
| `connectors` | `ConnectorDescriptor` (protocol id, contract revision, display name, transport kind `polling`, operations `identify` / `receive` / `send`, source), `ConnectorTransport` (host-implemented), `ConnectorFailure` / `ConnectorErrorKind`, and an immutable `ConnectorRegistry` metadata catalog. Descriptors never carry credentials or agent bindings. |
| `community_bundles` | `CommunityManifest` (schema version, id, version, compatibility, requested permissions, attribution, up to 4 components: at most 2 MCP and 2 skill). Manifests are at most 128 KiB; a bundle describes content and requested permissions and confers no authority. |
| `document_content` | `DocumentFormat` (`Docx`, `Pdf`, `Xlsx`), locators and `ExtractedDocumentText`, with bounds: 16 KiB rendered text, at most 10 snapshots (2 usable), 100 PDF pages, 16 XLSX sheets, 2,000 XLSX cells |
| `audio_content`, `speech` | `TranscriptionPort`, `SpeechPort`, WAV validation, duration and size bounds |
| `context` | `ServiceTokenEstimator`: ordinary engine token costs plus the exact derived document text sent to the model (document bytes are never discounted by calibration) |

## anima-document-content

`extract_document(format, bytes)` dispatches to `extract_docx`, `extract_pdf` or `extract_xlsx`. It uses `rawzip`, `quick-xml`, `flate2` and `pdf-extract`, and exposes no filesystem, process, network, OCR or password APIs. XLSX extraction reads stored cells and hidden-sheet metadata; it never evaluates formulas.

The crate's own warning matters: PDF dependencies build internal objects, so input and output bounds and panic containment **do not bound their memory or wall time**. Production callers must run extraction in a physically limited, owned worker process. The daemon does: `anima-daemon --document-worker-v2` is the worker entry point (`src/main.rs`), run under the daemon's admission and deadline policy (Windows only today; other hosts report document extraction as unavailable).

## anima-process

Process custody: launch a program so its whole process tree can be stopped and proven gone.

- `Custody::prepare(executable, args)` builds the containment and the command. `Containment` reports the guarantee: `JobObject` (Windows background commands), `Cgroup` (Linux with a delegated cgroup v2), `ProcessGroup` (macOS and Linux without delegation; a descendant that calls `setsid` escapes) or `ProcessTree` (Windows app sessions, killed with `taskkill /T /F`; a descendant whose parent already exited is missed).
- `session::AppSession` runs a program on a real terminal: ConPTY on Windows, a PTY elsewhere (`portable-pty`), with a `vt100` screen model. `AppSession::start(AppSessionConfig)`, `send(text, keys)`, `screen()`, `output_since(cursor, max_bytes)`, `wait(from, WaitFor)` (text, regex, or output settled), `resize`, `exit`, `idle_for`, `stop`. On Unix the session answers terminal queries that full-screen apps block on (cursor position, size, status, device attributes).

The daemon's `app_start` / `app_send` / `app_read` / `app_stop` and `bg_*` tools are built on it. See [Coding Apps and Helpers](/hosts/rust-daemon/coding/).

## anima-acp

A host-agnostic client for the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com): drive a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI through their ACP adapters) with typed events, real cancel, and permission requests routed to the host's own approvals.

- Why its own JSON-RPC (`rpc.rs`) rather than Zed's crate: that crate brings a different runtime stack and spawns the agent itself, while every owner-launched program here must run under `anima_process::Custody` so Stop can prove the tree gone.
- Implemented client surface: `initialize`, `session/new` and `session/load`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/update`, and serving `fs/read_text_file`, `fs/write_text_file` and `session/request_permission`. Unknown fields are ignored. No `terminal/*` is offered (agents use their own shell, inside the custody tree). `authenticate` is never called: an agent that needs a login surfaces as `AcpError::AuthRequired`.
- API: `AcpSession::start(AcpLaunch, Arc<dyn AcpClientHost>)`, `prompt(text) -> PromptHandle`, `wait`, `status`, `events_since(cursor)`, `cancel`, `stop`. The host implements `AcpClientHost` (file access, permission decisions). A fake agent binary (`fake-acp-agent`) backs the crate's tests only.

## anima-worktree

Creates and inspects git worktrees for helper agents by driving the `git` CLI through a hardened wrapper (hooks, fsmonitor, filters, pagers, credential helpers and global config disabled; 30-second default timeout per call).

- Layout: `<repo top level>/.worktrees/anima-helper-<name>` on branch `anima-helper/<name>`, from the current `HEAD`. `.worktrees/` is excluded through `<git-common-dir>/info/exclude`, so no tracked file changes. Names match `[a-z0-9-]{1,40}`.
- `Worktrees::create(repo_dir, name)`, `inspect(&Worktree) -> Outcome` (changed files up to 200, `git diff --stat` up to 8 KiB, `is_clean()`), `finish` (remove a clean worktree and branch, keep one with work) and `sweep(repo_dir, live)` for stale clean ones.

The daemon wires it to `spawn_helper` / `spawn_helper_async` with `worktree: true`.

## Tests

```bash
cargo test -p anima-service-adapters -p anima-document-content -p anima-process -p anima-acp -p anima-worktree
```

Process and PTY tests spawn real short-lived processes; worktree tests use temporary git repositories.
Why animaOS uses Rust for the engine and the host

The engine and the host are Rust. The TypeScript packages (`sdk`, `cli`, `tui`, `ui`, `apps/web`) are clients. This page records the reasons and the costs. It makes no benchmark claims; where numbers matter, measure.

## Why the Engine Is Rust

**One deployable binary.** The daemon (`anima-daemon`) and the packaged `anima` program are single executables. `anima` embeds the web console and updates itself, which would be much heavier to ship with a JavaScript runtime.

**Predictable resource use for long-lived work.** The daemon holds many things open at once: concurrent agent runs (default limit 8), SSE streams, background processes, PTY app sessions, connector pollers and in-memory memory indexes. A language with no garbage collector makes that footprint easier to reason about.

**Types as contracts.** The core states its boundaries as traits and data types: `ModelAdapter`, `Provider`, `Evaluator`, `DatabaseAdapter`, `MemoryVectorIndex`, `ExternalMemoryProvider`, `ExecutionStore`, `CapabilityExecutor`. Hosts implement them; the engine does not know which implementation it runs against. The compiler enforces that no I/O dependency creeps into `anima-core`: check its `Cargo.toml`. It has no HTTP client, no database driver and no async runtime (`tokio` is a dev-dependency only).

**Safety in code that handles secrets and processes.** The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (root `Cargo.toml`). The daemon manages credentials, child processes and filesystem writes on the owner's behalf; ownership and borrowing rules remove whole classes of data races and use-after-free bugs from that code. Where the OS offers no safe API (for example putting a Windows ConPTY child in a Job Object), the code documents the limit instead of reaching for `unsafe`: see [Coding Apps and Helpers](/hosts/rust-daemon/coding/).

## Pure Core, Real Host

`anima-core` and `anima-memory` operate on in-memory values and traits. The memory manager serializes to a `MemoryManagerSnapshot` that the host persists (JSON, SQLite or Postgres); the core never touches a file.

```rust
// the host decides where these bytes go
let snapshot = manager.snapshot();
```

Not every crate is I/O-free. `anima-model-adapters` makes HTTP calls with `reqwest`, `anima-process` spawns processes and PTYs, `anima-acp` talks to child processes, and `anima-worktree` drives the `git` CLI. They are in `packages/core-rust` because other hosts could reuse them, not because they are pure. See [Rust Core](/architecture/rust-core/).

## Why Not Everything in Rust

| Layer | Language | Reason |
|-------|----------|--------|
| Engine and host | Rust | Single binary, long-lived process, explicit boundaries |
| SDK, CLI, TUI | TypeScript | Familiar async patterns, Ink for terminal UI |
| Web console, playground | TypeScript | React ecosystem, Vite tooling |
| Docs sites | Astro | Starlight |

The SDK owns the request/response types shared by the CLI, TUI and UI. A client in another language only needs the daemon's HTTP/SSE contract (`/openapi.json` on a running daemon).

## Trade-offs

## Startup Sequence

`run_from_env` then `serve_with`:

1. Validate `ANIMAOS_RS_KEYCHAIN_NAMESPACE`, initialize `tracing` (redacted in-memory log tail plus console), read `ANIMAOS_RS_HOST` / `ANIMAOS_RS_PORT`, parse the `ANIMAOS_RS_*` limits (`config_from_env`; invalid values fail startup), bind the listener and log `anima-daemon listening`.
2. Install the external memory provider (`ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_PROVIDER`; an unknown id stops boot), validate the Python tool bridge path (`ANIMAOS_RS_TOOL_RPC_PYTHON_PATH`), the checkpoint root (`ANIMAOS_RS_CHECKPOINT_ROOT`; absolute, and Windows only) and the browser config (`ANIMAOS_RS_BROWSER_CONFIG_FILE`).
3. Create ChatGPT auth, open the provider key pool, build `RuntimeModelAdapter` from the environment.
4. `configure_persistence`: connect to Postgres and run migrations when `ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE=postgres` (failure stops boot); choose and load the memory store; configure embeddings; load the control-plane store, upgrading it with a backup if needed; choose and open the history store; rewrite the core-memory file copies. See [Persistence](/hosts/rust-daemon/persistence/).
5. Start the background embedding model load (served daemon only).
6. Build the runtime services and router, then start restored workers in this order: job recovery, Telegram connectors, Discord connectors, Drive, the scheduler, and the skills scanner (rescans at startup and every 60 seconds). A background sweep removes stale clean helper worktrees.
7. Serve until Ctrl+C, SIGTERM or `POST /api/system/shutdown`.

## Request Boundary

Order of layers (`routes/mod.rs`): request id (`x-request-id` generated or propagated) and a tracing span per request; per-route-group timeouts; the optional API-key gate; cache protection on connector callback routes.

- **Timeouts.** Standard routes use `ANIMAOS_RS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 30). The blocking run routes (`/api/agents/{id}/run`, `/api/swarms/{id}/run`, `/api/agents/{id}/messages`, connector sends, `/api/agencies/generate`) use `ANIMAOS_RS_RUN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 600). Voice and speech routes have their own bounds. A timeout returns `408`; an admitted run keeps going.
- **Body limit.** `ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (default 64 KiB) is enforced by handlers through a bounded body reader, not by a global layer; some routes (uploads, skill import, session runs) apply their own larger limits.
- **API key.** If `ANIMAOS_RS_API_KEY` is set, every route except health, readiness, metrics, `/openapi.json`, `/docs` and the exact OAuth callback paths requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key`. Unset means trust-the-network, fine only for loopback.
- **Owner authorization.** Most routes that read or change a person's data are *owner-only* (`LocalOwnerPolicy` in `routes/http.rs`). A request qualifies only if the daemon is bound to a loopback address, the `Host` header is loopback and no forwarding headers are present (`Forwarded`, `Via`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP`, `Client-IP`, `True-Client-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`), and then one of: an `Origin` header that exactly matches an allowed browser origin (`http://localhost:4200`, `127.0.0.1:4200`, `4201`, plus `ANIMA_ALLOWED_UI_ORIGINS`; only the configured ones when `ANIMA_SUPERVISOR_URL` is set), or `Authorization: Bearer <ANIMA_LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN>` for originless clients. Read-only fetches may omit `Origin` when Fetch Metadata says `same-origin` and the referrer is an allowed origin. Lifecycle routes additionally need a console session. A non-loopback bind therefore makes owner-only routes answer `403`; this is deliberate and is why the VPS package keeps the daemon on loopback behind a gateway (see [Staging Deployment](/hosts/rust-daemon/staging/)).

## State and Concurrency

All mutable state lives in `DaemonState` behind one `Arc<RwLock<..>>` (`SharedDaemonState`). Services hold weak or shared references; locks are not held across network or persistence waits. Run admission is bounded by a semaphore (`ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`, default 8) plus a per-agent limit (`ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_RUNS_PER_AGENT`, default 3, 1 to 64). Control-plane changes go through a single transaction mutex in `AgentRunCoordinator` so snapshots stay consistent.

## Graceful Shutdown

Ctrl+C or Unix SIGTERM (or the drain route's shutdown) starts a 40-second budget (`SHUTDOWN_BUDGET`). Producers close first: no new runs, jobs, schedule fires or connector admissions. Then admitted work drains (the run coordinator gives running runs up to 30 seconds to commit), connectors and the scheduler stop, the browser service closes, and the history worker does a final flush. Live SSE streams are closed first so open tabs never block exit. Work still unsettled when the budget expires is left for the next boot to mark `interrupted`, and a warning says admitted work may have uncertain effects. Memory snapshots are written as memory changes happen, not at shutdown.

## Rules for Contributors

- Reusable engine code belongs in `packages/core-rust`, not here.
- Do not add a tool without a risk class (see `approvals/policy.rs`).
- Never put secrets in the control plane, logs or model-visible text. Credentials go through the OS credential store (`keychain.rs`, `connectors/credentials.rs`).
- Every new owner route needs the owner-authorization check and `Cache-Control: no-store`, an entry in the OpenAPI registration and a handler test.
- For host changes run `bun x nx run rust-daemon:test --skipNxCache`.
Route families, conventions, authorization and key request shapes of the Rust daemon

The daemon serves operational endpoints, `/api/*` application endpoints and a Scalar API explorer at `/docs`. This page is a map and a set of conventions. For the exhaustive route list use the generated inventory in `hosts/rust-daemon/README.md` (it follows `ApiDoc::openapi()` and is checked against the router) or `GET /openapi.json` on a running daemon; per-route limits and error codes are documented there and enforced by handler tests. The TypeScript SDK (`packages/sdk`) is the reference client.

## Conventions

- **JSON is camelCase** everywhere (`agentId`, `createdAtMs`, `maxTurns`, `tokenUsage`). Several request types reject unknown fields.
- **Envelopes.** Lists and single resources are wrapped: `{ agents: [...] }`, `{ agent: {...} }`, `{ swarm: {...} }`, `{ results: [...] }`, `{ memories: [...] }`, `{ session }`, `{ run }`.
- **Errors** are `{ "error": "message" }` (some families add a machine `code`). Common statuses: `400` validation, `403` `local owner authorization required`, `404`, `408` timeout, `409` conflict or stale revision, `429` rate or queue limit, `503` store unavailable or shutting down.
- **`x-request-id`** is returned on every response and propagated when sent.
- **Owner-only routes** answer `Cache-Control: no-store`. They require the owner authorization described in [Rust Daemon](/hosts/rust-daemon/#request-boundary). A client that is not a browser on an allowed origin sends `Authorization: Bearer <ANIMA_LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN>`.
- **Optional API key.** With `ANIMAOS_RS_API_KEY` set, every non-exempt route also needs `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key` with that key.
- **Idempotency.** Session run submission requires an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 128 visible ASCII characters, remembered for 24 hours).

## Agents

```http
POST /api/agents
{
  "name": "researcher",
  "model": "gpt-4o",
  "provider": "openai",
  "system": "You are a research assistant.",
  "bio": "I find and synthesize information.",
  "tools": ["read_file", "web_fetch"],
  "settings": { "temperature": 0.2, "maxTokens": 2048, "maxToolIterations": 8 },
  "fallbacks": [{ "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5" }]
}
```

`tools` entries are names or objects `{ name, description, parameters, examples }`. `fallbacks` allows at most 3 entries, none equal to the agent's own provider and model. The response is `201 { agent }`:

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "state": {
      "id": "agent-1-...", "name": "researcher", "status": "idle",
      "config": { "name": "researcher", "model": "gpt-4o", "provider": "openai", "...": "..." },
      "createdAtMs": 1760000000000,
      "tokenUsage": { "promptTokens": 0, "completionTokens": 0, "totalTokens": 0 }
    },
    "messageCount": 0, "messages": [], "eventCount": 0, "lastTask": null
  }
}
```

`GET /api/agents?view=summary` omits `messages`. `PATCH /api/agents/{id}` updates `name`, `model`, `provider`, `system`, `tools` and `fallbacks` (at least one field). `messages` and `messageCount` cover only the hot tail (see [Persistence](/hosts/rust-daemon/persistence/#history-store)); session routes cover the full history.

{ "text": "What are the main types of neural networks?" }

The call blocks until completion or the run timeout and returns `{ agent, result }` where `result` is `{ "status": "success" | "error", "data": { "text": "..." }, "error": null, "durationMs": 2500 }`. After a `408` the admitted run continues. New clients should use session runs (below).

An agent uses the computer through general tools plus know-how (skills); no app has a built-in integration. This page maps those tools to their source and states the guarantees and gaps. Libraries: `anima-process`, `anima-acp`, `anima-worktree` ([Supporting Crates](/architecture/rust-core/supporting-crates/)). Daemon code: `tools/process.rs` and `tools/process/`, `agent_runs/worktrees.rs`, `agent_runs/async_helpers.rs`, `coding_apps.rs`, `coding_keys.rs`, `foreign_sessions/`, `tool_rpc/`, `filesystem_checkpoints/`. Per-feature limits are in `hosts/rust-daemon/README.md` ("Using apps", "Autonomous runtime").

## Approvals

`bash`, `bg_start`, `bg_stop`, `app_start`, `app_send`, `app_stop`, `acp_start`, `acp_prompt`, `acp_cancel`, `acp_stop` and `execute_code` are **exec** class. With the daemon default (`exec: ask`) each waits for the owner. A command-prefix rule such as "allow `claude`" covers `bash`, `bg_start`, `app_start` and `acp_start`. Picking **Operate** in settings or onboarding also sets `exec: allow`. Read tools (`bg_list`, `bg_output`, `bg_wait`, `app_read`, `app_list`, `acp_read`, `acp_list`) never ask. See [Runs and Sessions](/hosts/rust-daemon/runs/#approvals).

A rule for an HTTP client, interpreter, shell, package runner or git lets the agent act as the owner on the machine, including changing its own approval policy through the loopback API. Keep exec rules narrow.

## Background Commands

`bg_start` runs a command under process custody (`anima_process::Custody`) with a shell allowlist environment plus `PAGER=cat` and `GIT_PAGER=cat`. At most `ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` (default 8) run at once. `bg_wait` blocks until a job exits, prints a pattern, or times out (at most 120 seconds). A job that ends on its own wakes the agent in the conversation that started it, unless the agent already saw the exit or stopped it. `notify_on` (up to 4 texts or `/regex/`) wakes it once per pattern when a new output line matches while the job keeps running.

## App Sessions

`app_start` opens a program on a real terminal (ConPTY on Windows, a PTY elsewhere, 120 by 40 by default). `app_send` types text and named keys (multi-line text goes in as one bracketed paste when the app asks for it); `app_read` returns the visible screen and new output and can wait for text or for output to settle; `app_stop` ends the app and its tree. Limits: 1 MiB transcript (2,000 lines), 2,000 lines of scrollback, 16 KiB per read.

## ACP Coding Agents

`acp_start` runs any Agent Client Protocol agent (`npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`, `codex-acp`, `opencode acp`, `gemini --acp`); `acp_prompt`, `acp_read`, `acp_cancel` and `acp_stop` drive it. Its permission requests become ordinary approvals with their own tool names, judged by the same policy and rules:

| ACP request | Approval tool | Class |
|-------------|---------------|-------|
| edit, delete, move | `acp_edit` | write |
| run a command | `acp_execute` | exec |
| fetch | `acp_fetch` | network |
| anything else | `acp_other` | exec |

Reads never ask and Anima never answers "allow always" on the owner's behalf. When an agent offers session modes, Anima switches it to its asking mode (`default` for Claude Code) so it asks before editing. File reads and writes by the agent are confined to the session folder. An agent that needs a sign-in reports it (`AuthRequired`); Anima never signs in for the owner.

## Sessions and Keys

At most 4 app and coding-agent sessions per agent, both kinds together (`MAX_LIVE_PER_AGENT`). They outlive a run, stop after 30 minutes idle and die with the daemon. The chat shows each as a live card with Stop (and Cancel turn for coding agents); routes `POST /api/agents/{id}/app-sessions/{sid}/stop` and `acp-sessions/{sid}/stop|cancel`.

Coding apps use their own sign-in by default. Per agent, the owner may pass through `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (`GET` / `PUT /api/agents/{id}/coding-keys`). The values come from the daemon's own environment and never pass through the model; off by default. The owner's choices are saved with the approval policies, which agents cannot write.

`GET /api/coding-apps` reports which of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI are on `PATH` and start, with the know-how bundle for each (`bundles/coding-agents/<app>/manifest.json`, compiled into the daemon). Installing a bundle still goes through the community-bundle review.

## Containment

| Platform | Background commands | App sessions |
|----------|---------------------|--------------|
| Windows | Job Object: every descendant is contained | ConPTY children cannot join a Job Object without `unsafe`; Stop runs `taskkill /T /F`, and a descendant whose parent already exited is missed |
| Linux with delegated cgroup v2 | cgroup leaf: every descendant is contained | same |
| macOS, Linux without delegation | process group: a descendant that calls `setsid` escapes | same |

## Helpers and Worktrees

An agent can delegate to **helpers**: `spawn_helper` (synchronous) and `spawn_helper_async` with `list_helper_runs`, `steer_helper`, `stop_helper`. Helpers answer to their companion's policy and rules but never wait for approval (a call that would ask is denied). Four starts or helpers are shared between synchronous and asynchronous delegation. Async assignments have at most eight tool turns, two minutes of execution and eight accepted steers; a launch returns a saved run handle, and the parent must inspect the settled result before claiming completion. A restart closes uncertain helper work for review instead of replaying it, and stop does not undo completed effects.

`worktree: true` (and an optional workspace-relative `repo`, default `.`) gives the helper its own git worktree at `<repo top level>/.worktrees/anima-helper-<id>` on branch `anima-helper/<id>` from the current `HEAD` (`anima-worktree`). Its file tools work there; agent files, memory and attachments keep the global workspace; the shared task-list tools are removed. Helpers cannot run git; the daemon makes every git call itself with hooks, fsmonitor, filters, pagers, credential helpers and global config disabled and a 30-second limit. Outside a git repository with at least one commit the spawn is refused; it never falls back to the shared checkout. When the helper's run ends the daemon inspects the worktree: untouched worktrees and branches are removed, others are kept and the parent receives a `worktree` object (path, branch, base commit, changed files, diff stat, how to review, merge or remove). At startup it sweeps clean helper worktrees with no unmerged commits.

## Code Execution

`execute_code` runs a Python program through a bridge (`tool_rpc/`). It is off unless `ANIMAOS_RS_TOOL_RPC_PYTHON_PATH` points at an existing absolute Python 3.10+ interpreter (Windows profile today; no PATH discovery, no installation) and the agent has both `execute_code` and `bash` plus any native tools the program needs. Programs import their captured tool intersection from `anima_tools`; every native call keeps its own validation, approval and durable receipt. Each execution starts fresh; four physical cells are shared by the host, one per agent and session, with a 5-minute maximum. Helpers, recursion, browser and MCP calls and background-process tools are excluded. This is approved arbitrary local execution with the owner's OS access, not a sandbox. Portable bounds are in `anima-core::tool_rpc` (64 KiB of code, 50 calls).

## Native-File Recovery (Windows)

With `ANIMAOS_RS_CHECKPOINT_ROOT` set (an absolute private directory outside the workspace), `write_file`, `edit_file` and `multi_edit` save an exact preimage before changing one ordinary file and return a `filesystemCheckpointId`; `checkpoint_list` and `checkpoint_restore` (granted separately) recover it. One checkpoint covers one native action, not a turn or a shell command. Limits: 10 MiB per file, 64 MiB capture content, 500 MiB store, 20 records per namespace; no automatic pruning. Missing or corrupt evidence reports `Filesystem checkpoint RecoveryRequired` and stops further native effects in that run. On other platforms setting the variable fails startup.

## Importing Claude Code and Codex Conversations

`GET /api/foreign-sessions?source=claude-code|codex` lists logs newest first (50 per page), `.../{handle}/preview` shows the newest 40 messages, and `POST /api/agents/{id}/foreign-sessions/{handle}/import` turns one into an ordinary chat (`origin: "import"`, titled `Imported · <title>`). Sources: Claude Code `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/*/*.jsonl` (else `~/.claude/projects`), Codex `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` (else `~/.codex/sessions`). Logs are only read; a handle is the SHA-256 of the resolved path, so paths are never accepted or returned. Logs over 32 MiB are refused; at most 2,000 messages (the newest) are imported, each cut to 16 KiB. Re-importing the same conversation returns the existing session (`alreadyImported: true`). Telegram, Discord, Google Drive, Calendar, mail, MCP and OAuth apps in the Rust daemon

Connectors are host features in `hosts/rust-daemon/src/connectors/` (plus `mcp/`). They run **inside the daemon**: polling, pairing, delivery, persistence and restart recovery have no second process. Restored, enabled connectors start at boot after job recovery (`start_restored`). Credentials come from the OS credential store; connector records in the control plane never contain secrets.

The portable contract (descriptors, `ConnectorTransport`, bounds) is in `anima-service-adapters` (see [Supporting Crates](/architecture/rust-core/supporting-crates/)). `hosts/rust-daemon/CONNECTOR-CONTRIBUTING.md` is the contributor guide for adding a transport.

## Trust Model

- **Reviewed source only.** Community connectors are source contributions compiled into the host. They run with host privileges and need a rebuild. There is no installer, dynamic ABI, WASM loader or sandbox. Installable modules are deferred.
- **Descriptors are passive.** The `ConnectorRegistry` (`connectors/registry.rs`) is an immutable metadata catalog; registering a descriptor discovers, activates and authorizes nothing.
- **Remote input is never authority.** Sender ids, message ids and channel ids are native strings and never grant tool access. The owner decides which chats and users may talk to an agent.
- **Owner routes only.** Every connector management route is owner-authorized, `no-store`, and (apart from OAuth callbacks) needs an approved origin or admin token. See [Rust Daemon](/hosts/rust-daemon/#request-boundary).

## Telegram

Code: `connectors/telegram.rs` (client), `connectors/runtime/` (manager, workers, inbound, delivery, processing, owner turns), `connectors/adapters/telegram.rs` (transport bridge).

- **Setup.** `POST /api/agents/{id}/connectors/telegram` validates a bot token with Telegram, stores the token in the credential store and saves a record (bot identity, room id, state). `PUT .../connectors/{connector_id}/credential` replaces the token; `restart`, `messages` (list), `messages` (send) and `DELETE` complete the lifecycle. There is no shared token environment variable, and the same bot can be connected to only one copy (dev or installed) at a time.
- **Pairing.** A first message from an unknown chat creates a pending pairing candidate (valid 10 minutes); the owner approves one chat with `POST .../pairings/{chat_id}/approve`. Only the approved chat can reach the agent.
- **Intake.** A long-poll worker per connector reads updates, with exponential retry (100 ms up to 30 s) and a 60-second wait when Telegram reports another poller. Inbound updates are admitted durably before the agent runs, and the cursor (`nextUpdateId`) advances with them.
- **Runs.** A message in the paired private chat runs the agent's owner turn in a dedicated session (`kind: telegram`, source `telegram`). Groups and shared chats do not count as owner turns for conversation reviews. An approval requested by a Telegram-started run waits 15 minutes, not 30, because the connector handles one message at a time.
- **Delivery.** Replies are recorded in an outbound journal and delivered at least once. Network success followed by a failed save is uncertain and may be retried; a retry reuses the stored text and does not run the model again. A stopped Telegram run whose reply is not yet delivered suppresses it.
- **Retention.** Delivered rows are kept 7 days (at most 1,000).

## Discord

Code: `connectors/discord/`, `connectors/adapters/discord.rs`.

- **Scope.** One guild text channel per connection plus a non-empty list of permitted user ids. One agent can have several connections, even the same bot in different channels; each has its own conversation, cursor, credential and delivery journal. A second non-deleted connection for the same agent and channel is rejected. Channel or user changes mean disconnect and recreate.
- **Activation.** New records are saved **disabled**. First activation records a latest-message baseline so earlier history is never dispatched; later enables resume from the saved cursor. Routes: `POST .../connectors/discord`, `PATCH .../discord/{id}`, `PUT .../discord/{id}/credential`, `activate`, `restart`, `retry`, `outbound/suppress`, `DELETE`.
- **Intake.** A persistent Gateway connection (`twilight-gateway`, owned independently of model runs) signals readiness and channel activity (`GatewaySignal` carries only guild and channel ids). Messages are read through the REST channel API with a bounded backward catch-up that must prove it reached the saved cursor before receipts and the cursor are committed together. An unproven or oversized backlog pauses visibly. Bot, self, webhook and unsupported messages never run the agent. Gateway identify attempts share pacing per verified bot id.
- **Delivery.** Each reply chunk has a durable send intent and receipt; at most 8 chunks are sent, with a truncation notice if needed, and all mentions are disabled. Ambiguous or partial sends become `Unknown` and are never replayed automatically. Safe retry refuses `Unknown`; the owner checks Discord and explicitly suppresses the uncertain output.
- **Limits.** Edits, deletions, reactions, threads, slash commands and voice are not observed; a message deleted before polling can be missed. Required bot permissions: View Channel, Read Message History, Send Messages (and the Message Content intent where the portal requires it).

## Google Drive, Calendar and Mail

All three share the OAuth app service (`connectors/oauth_apps.rs`). The owner configures a Google (and, for Outlook, Microsoft) OAuth application in the console (`GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE /api/connectors/oauth-apps/{provider}`) or through `ANIMA_GOOGLE_*` / `ANIMA_MICROSOFT_*` variables, and registers the exact callback URLs shown in the UI under `ANIMA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`:

| Service | Callback path |
|---------|---------------|
| Gmail | `/api/connectors/mail/gmail/callback` |
| Google Calendar | `/api/connectors/gcalendar/callback` |
| Google Drive | `/api/connectors/gdrive/callback` |
| Outlook | `/api/connectors/mail/outlook/callback` |

Callbacks are the only `GET` routes exempt from the API key and the owner check; they authenticate with an expiring, single-use OAuth state. Pending nonces and verifiers are in memory, so a restart invalidates an unfinished consent.

- **Drive** (`connectors/drive/`). On-demand native tools, not a messaging transport. The owner pastes 1 to 16 Drive or Docs links or ids and approves Google's `drive.readonly` scope; Anima then restricts that agent to its immutable selected ids. Only `drive_search` (selected file names) and `drive_read` exist: exact-id metadata, Google Docs exported as plain text, stored UTF-8 plain text, at most 1 MiB streamed and 32,768 characters returned, with source link, timestamps and digests. No listing, folder traversal, writes or indexing. Every read rechecks agent, connector generation, selected ids, account and tool grant. Disconnecting removes local authority and tokens but never revokes Google-wide access.
- **Calendar** (`connectors/gcalendar/`). OAuth connect, `calendar_list_events` and confirmation-gated writes: `calendar_create_event`, `calendar_update_event` and `calendar_delete_event` create pending write records (at most 50 per agent) that the owner approves or rejects (`.../writes/{write_id}/approve|reject`). There is no polling loop; proactive behavior uses ordinary scheduled prompts.
- **Mail** (`connectors/mail/`, providers `gmail` and `outlook`). `mail_list_messages` reads; `mail_create_draft` creates a local immutable draft. Sending happens only when the owner approves the draft through the owner route; agents cannot send.

Tokens for these services live in the credential store under generation-specific keys, separate per service.

## MCP

Code: `mcp/` (`records.rs`, `service.rs`, `transport.rs`, `stdio.rs`, `credentials.rs`), built on the `rmcp` client (fixed protocol `2025-11-25`). Reference: `docs/companion/mcp.md`.

- A connection is scoped to one ordinary agent: anonymous or Bearer-authenticated **Streamable HTTP** (HTTPS, or literal loopback HTTP; no redirects or proxies) or an explicitly started **local stdio** process (absolute executable path, at most 32 arguments, no shell strings; **Windows only**: on other platforms the stdio transport reports itself unavailable). At most 4 connections (`MAX_CONNECTIONS`) and 32 reviewed tools (`MAX_REVIEWED_TOOLS`) are kept.
- Saving, listing or restoring a connection starts nothing. The owner connects, discovers, **reviews** one exact descriptor (a digest check; no grant), then separately adds the reviewed alias to the agent's tool grants.
- Every external tool is classified as **exec** for approvals; server hints cannot lower it. The dispatcher captures the full reviewed descriptor, connection generation and grant epoch before approval and rechecks them before dispatch and before accepting the result. Helpers inherit no MCP grants.
- Routes under `/api/agents/{id}/mcp-connections`: create, list, get, patch (compare-and-swap on `expectedVersion`), `connect`, `discover`, `review`, `disconnect`, `PATCH .../grants/{alias}`, `PUT` / `DELETE .../credential`, `DELETE`.

## Health, Readiness and Status

| Endpoint | Auth | Use |
|----------|------|-----|
| `GET /health`, `/api/health` | none | Liveness. Always `200 {"status":"ok"}` |
| `GET /ready`, `/api/ready` | none | Readiness. `503` with `issues` when the daemon cannot serve |
| `GET /metrics` | none | Prometheus text, counts only |
| `GET /api/status` | owner | One snapshot of version, uptime, storage, providers, connectors, automations, approvals, runs, events, logs, limits |

Readiness reports `database: "missing"` and returns `503` when `ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE=postgres` is set without a working database adapter. It also reports an issue when the background-process manager is unavailable or the history store is failing, so orchestrators can retry or fail fast. A healthy proxy alone does not establish a healthy daemon or a configured model.

`/api/status` details: `buildRevision` is non-null only when the build set `ANIMAOS_BUILD_REVISION` at compile time; `storage` includes persistence mode, control-plane durability and the history store's health, queue sizes, redacted last error and flush-error count; `providers` says whether each provider is configured and never includes a key; `connectors` is capped at 50 entries and never includes a credential. A console talking to an older daemon without this route shows an update instruction.

## Control-Plane Durability

By default the daemon is an `ephemeral` control plane. Set `ANIMAOS_RS_CONTROL_PLANE_FILE` or run Postgres mode for restart recovery. Recovery restores registrations, sessions, the run ledger, approvals policy, connector records and the latest snapshots; **work that was running is restored as interrupted or failed and is never resumed mid-turn**. In Postgres mode, retried requests that repeat the same retry key can reuse completed tool steps from `step_log`. Full detail and upgrade backups: [Persistence](/hosts/rust-daemon/persistence/).

`GET /metrics` (`routes/health.rs`, `routes/status.rs`) is unauthenticated and carries counts only: no agent names, ids, prompts or costs.

|--------|---------|
| `anima_daemon_ready` | 1 when ready |
| `anima_daemon_uptime_seconds` | Process uptime |
| `anima_daemon_agents`, `anima_daemon_swarms`, `anima_daemon_swarm_snapshots`, `anima_daemon_memories` | Registered counts |
| `anima_daemon_runs`, `anima_daemon_runs_running`, `anima_daemon_runs_queued` | Run ledger counts (the ledger prunes old finished runs, so these are not lifetime totals) |
| `anima_daemon_approvals_pending` | Approvals waiting for the owner |
| `anima_daemon_automations_failing` | Automations in failure |
| `anima_daemon_background_processes`, `anima_daemon_background_process_manager_healthy` | Background command count and manager health |
| `anima_daemon_database_configured`, `anima_daemon_persistence_mode_info`, `anima_daemon_control_plane_durability_info` | Persistence configuration (labelled `mode`) |
| `anima_daemon_max_concurrent_runs`, `anima_daemon_max_background_processes`, `anima_daemon_max_request_bytes`, `anima_daemon_request_timeout_seconds` | Configured limits |

There are no HTTP request-count or latency metrics; use the request log lines (below).

## Logging

The daemon logs through `tracing`. The default filter is `anima_daemon=info,tower_http=info`; override with `RUST_LOG`. Each HTTP request gets a span with method, URI and `x-request-id`, and a response line with status and latency in milliseconds. The daemon sets `x-request-id` on every response and propagates a client-supplied one, so client and server logs can be correlated.

An in-memory tail keeps the last 2,000 lines (each at most 4 KiB), redacted at capture (API keys, `Authorization` and bearer values, OAuth and Telegram tokens, JWTs and long unlabeled tokens become `[redacted]`). Redaction is pattern-based, so treat `RUST_LOG=debug` or `trace` with care: it lets request and provider payload fragments into both the console and the tail.

| Route | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `GET /api/logs?level=&q=&after=&limit=` | Owner. `{ lines, newestSeq }`; `limit` 1 to 1,000 (default 200) |
| `GET /api/logs/stream?level=&q=&after=` | Owner SSE: `event: log` per line, `event: resync` when the stream fell behind; at most 8 streams |

`anima logs [-f]` (packaged program) reads the supervisor's log files instead.

## Drain, Shutdown and the Supervisor Relay

Before Stop, Restart, Quit or Update a supervisor drains the daemon so no agent work is cut off (`system/drain.rs`):

| Route | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `POST /api/system/drain` | Begin draining; `202 { draining, inFlight }` |
| `GET /api/system/drain` | `{ draining, inFlight }` where `inFlight` counts chat runs, queued runs, swarm runs, helper runs, jobs, background processes, app sessions and ACP sessions |
| `DELETE /api/system/drain` | Cancel the drain; `204` |
| `POST /api/system/shutdown` | `202`, then the same graceful shutdown as SIGTERM |
| `GET /api/system`, `POST /api/system/actions/{action}` | Relay to the supervisor (`start`, `stop`, `restart`, `quit`, `update`, `check-update`, `cancel`); `supervised: false` when no supervisor is configured |
| `POST /api/system/session` | Trade the one-time console launch code (valid 15 seconds) for a 12-hour console session |

While draining, new chat messages, legacy runs, peer messages, connector sends, swarm runs, jobs and goals are refused with `503`; Telegram and Discord messages are still received, and due automations and queued jobs stay due. Accepted runs finish. Authorization: without an `Origin`, the admin bearer token (`ANIMA_LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN`); from a browser, an allowed Origin plus a console session (cookie `anima_console_<port>` and the `x-anima-console-session` header), because any local process can send an Origin header. See [Packaged Anima](/packaged-anima/) for the console-session model and its stated limits.

The daemon's control plane, history store, memory store, key pool and credential storage, plus upgrades and rollback

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The daemon keeps durable state in four places, chosen independently at startup (`app/persistence.rs`, `configure_persistence`):

| Store | What it holds | Backends | Source |
|-------|---------------|----------|--------|
| **Control plane** | Agents and their runtime snapshots, swarms, sessions (hot tail), the run ledger, approval policies and rules, skills registry and drafts, automations, jobs and goals, connector records (never secrets), workspace settings, pricing overrides, side-task model, MCP and bundle records, learning state | JSON file, or Postgres `host_snapshots` row `control_plane` | `control_plane_store.rs` |
| **History store** | Full message transcripts, finished runs, usage rows, decided approvals, automation fire records, attachment metadata | SQLite, Postgres `history_*` tables, or in memory | `history/` |
| **Memory store** | The `MemoryManager` snapshot (memories, entities, relationships, temporal facts) and, separately, embedding vectors | JSON file, SQLite, or Postgres `host_snapshots` row `memory` | `memory_store.rs`, `memory_embeddings.rs` |
| **Step log** | Tool-step records that let a retried request reuse completed tool results | Postgres `step_log` only | `postgres.rs` |

Two more things are durable but are not "stores": the **provider key pool** file and **credentials** in the OS credential store. Everything else (live runtimes, SSE streams, PTY and ACP sessions, MCP connections, browser scopes, pending approvals) is process memory and is gone after a restart.

## Persistence Modes

`ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE`:

- `memory` (default): no Postgres. The control plane is **ephemeral** unless `ANIMAOS_RS_CONTROL_PLANE_FILE` is set. Despite the name, file stores are still honored in this mode: the VPS package runs in `memory` mode with explicit files under `/state`.
- `postgres`: requires `DATABASE_URL`; connects, runs the embedded migrations in `migrations/` (`step_log` and `host_snapshots`; relaxed step-index uniqueness; `history_*` tables) and **refuses to start** if any step fails. Postgres becomes the default home of the control plane and the memory snapshot, unless an explicit file variable is set.

`/ready` reports `controlPlaneDurability` (`ephemeral`, `json`, `postgres`) and `database` (`configured`, `disabled`, `missing`).

## Control Plane

`CONTROL_PLANE_STORE_VERSION` is currently **21** (`control_plane_store.rs`). The snapshot is versioned JSON written atomically (temporary file plus rename for JSON, a transaction for Postgres). On load:

- A snapshot **newer** than the running daemon is refused (`unsupported control plane store version`).
- An **older** snapshot is upgraded. Before saving the new version the daemon writes a backup. In JSON mode this is `<control-plane-file>.pre-<feature>.bak` (for example `.pre-sessions.bak`, `.pre-approvals.bak`, `.pre-discord.bak`, `.pre-drive.bak`; the suffix constants sit at the top of the file). In Postgres mode it is the `control_plane.backup.<old version>` row of `host_snapshots`. If the backup cannot be written the daemon refuses to boot and leaves the snapshot untouched. An existing earlier backup is never overwritten by a later upgrade.
- Anything that was `running` when the process died is restored as failed or interrupted; a model turn is never resumed mid-way.

### Restore consistency

A rollback is a set of stores, not one file. The control-plane backup is only a component: restoring it alone while leaving a newer history store can resurrect rows later. For a rollback, stop the daemon and restore the matching generation of control plane, history, memory, workspace and uploads, and the credential store together, with the recorded binaries and (in the VPS package) the original keyring password. Changes made since the backup are lost. Do not edit snapshot versions by hand, and do not apply old per-milestone SQL notes from the README to a current store. `deploy/vps/README.md` has the full backup and restore procedure.

## History Store

Every committed message and every terminal run is written through an **outbox** to the history store (`history/outbox.rs`), which a `HistoryWorker` flushes in the background and on shutdown, and which prunes the control plane's hot tail every 10 minutes (`sessions/pruning.rs`). The store is append-oriented and row-based, so session reads, message search, exports and old runs do not depend on the control plane keeping everything.

| Choice | When |
|--------|------|
| SQLite at `ANIMAOS_RS_HISTORY_SQLITE_FILE` | explicit |
| SQLite at `history.sqlite` beside the control-plane file | a control-plane file is set and no explicit path |
| Postgres tables `history_messages`, `history_runs`, `history_usage`, `history_approvals`, `history_schedule_runs`, `history_attachments` | Postgres control plane and no explicit SQLite file |
| In memory, 100,000 rows per table (`EPHEMERAL_HISTORY_MAX_ROWS`) | otherwise; nothing is pruned from the control plane |

A history file that cannot be opened refuses boot before the control-plane snapshot is touched. `/api/status` reports the store's health, queue size, the last (redacted) error and a flush-error count; `/ready` reports `not_ready` while it is failing. Search tokenizes at most 8 words per query and indexes at most 64 KiB of text per message (the full record is never truncated). The Postgres history tables need **Postgres 12 or newer** because `history_messages.search` is a generated column; rolling back across the history migration (`20260923000000_history_store.sql`) also needs its `_sqlx_migrations` row removed and the `history_*` tables moved aside, since sqlx refuses to start with a missing applied migration.

Deleting sessions or agents records a durable **history deletion** that is replayed at boot, so a crash between the control-plane save and the history delete does not resurrect data.

## Memory Store and Embeddings

Choice and defaults are in [Memory in the Daemon](/architecture/rust-core/anima-memory/daemon-memory/#stores-and-persistence) and [Environment](/hosts/rust-daemon/env/#persistence): explicit JSON or SQLite file, else Postgres, else `memory.sqlite` beside the control-plane file, else memory-only. Writes autosave after memory routes, tools, reviews and retention runs. Vectors go to `memory_embeddings` tables in the same SQLite file (or `ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_SQLITE_FILE`); in Postgres staging they are process-local and rebuilt from the snapshot on boot.

## Provider Key Pool

`provider_keys/` holds a pool of API keys per provider with rotation: a key that fails for a key-specific reason (rate limit, overload, billing, auth) rests and the call moves to the next ready key. The rest is the provider's own retry time for rate limits and overload; an hour for billing; 5 minutes for a rejected key; 60 seconds for any other failure on the only usable key; otherwise an hour; never more than 24 hours. The environment key is always key `env`, listed first, and is never written to the file. Keys are returned masked. Selection strategies: `fill_first` (default), `round_robin`, `random`, `least_used`. The file is `ANIMAOS_RS_PROVIDER_KEYS_FILE`, else `provider-keys.json` beside the control-plane file, else keys last until restart (`persisted: false`). An unreadable or unsupported file is left untouched and the daemon runs on environment keys with a warning.

## Credentials

Secrets never enter the control plane, history, logs or model-visible text. They live in the OS credential store through the `keyring` crate (`keychain.rs`): Telegram and Discord bot tokens, Google and Microsoft connector tokens and OAuth app secrets, MCP credentials, and the ChatGPT subscription login (a single item on macOS and Linux; chunked on Windows because Credential Manager caps each secret at 2,560 bytes). `ANIMAOS_RS_KEYCHAIN_NAMESPACE` prefixes service names so an installed copy and a development copy never share or overwrite items. Debug builds on macOS are ad-hoc signed, so keychain "Always Allow" resets on every rebuild unless you sign with a stable identity (see [Local Development](/hosts/rust-daemon/local/)).

## Development Defaults

`bun dev` sets `ANIMAOS_RS_CONTROL_PLANE_FILE` to `~/.animaos-swarm/data/control-plane.json` (so `history.sqlite` and `memory.sqlite` land beside it) unless you set your own path, run Postgres mode, or set `ANIMAOS_DEV_EPHEMERAL=1`. This is `tools/workspace-dev/src/hosts.ts`.

<Aside type="caution" title="Same folder as the installed program">
  The packaged `anima` program keeps its data in `~/.animaos-swarm/data/` too, with the same file names. The dev loop and an installed copy therefore point at the same default files unless you override the path. They use different credential namespaces and ports, but not different data folders. Set `ANIMAOS_RS_CONTROL_PLANE_FILE` (and a matching `ANIMAOS_RS_PROVIDER_KEYS_FILE` if you add keys) to a project-local path, or `ANIMAOS_DEV_EPHEMERAL=1`, when you do not want to touch an installed copy's data.
</Aside>

## Postgres Staging Notes

Postgres mode stores the control plane and memory snapshot in `host_snapshots`, step logs in `step_log` and history in `history_*`. Run **one** daemon replica: vectors are process-local and several daemons would each hold their own run state and workers. See [Staging Deployment](/hosts/rust-daemon/staging/).
Sessions, the run ledger, steer and stop, approvals, live events, jobs and automations in the Rust daemon

This is the daemon's conversation machinery. Behavior lives in `agent_runs.rs` and `agent_runs/` (the `AgentRunCoordinator`), `runs/ledger.rs`, `sessions/`, `approvals/`, `live/`, `jobs.rs` and `schedules.rs`. Exact per-route limits and error strings are in `hosts/rust-daemon/README.md`; the numbers below are the constants in source.

## Sessions

A session is one conversation room of one agent plus its record. Its id equals the room id (ids are up to 200 bytes of `A-Za-z0-9._:-`; legacy rooms map to a stable `legacy-room:<hash>` id).

| Kind | Created by |
|------|-----------|
| `chat` | The owner, through `POST /api/agents/{id}/sessions` (60 per agent per minute) |
| `telegram`, `discord` | A connector's dedicated thread |
| `checkin` | A schedule (room `schedule:<id>`) |
| `job` | A job's runs |
| `helper` | A helper agent's delegated work |

Titles are 1 to 120 characters; a new chat titled `New chat` takes its title from its first message, and the daemon generates AI titles for new chats (only the real daemon, never embedded or test constructors). `GET /api/agents/{id}/sessions/{sid}` also reports `contextUsage`, an estimate of the model-visible history plus the session summary against the context budget.

### Hot tail, history and context

Every committed message is mirrored to the [history store](/hosts/rust-daemon/persistence/#history-store). Every 10 minutes the daemon prunes mirrored messages from the control plane down to a **hot tail**: each session's newest 200 visible messages plus anything from the last 24 hours (never while a run in the session is active, never in ephemeral mode, and not while a Telegram delivery still needs the message). Agent snapshots show only the hot tail; session routes, search and export read the full history.

Each run sends the model the session's newest whole turns that fit its context budget: the agent setting `contextBudgetTokens`, else 60% of the model's context window capped at 200,000 tokens, else 32,000, less `maxTokens` (default 4,096, at most half the budget) reserved for the reply. Estimates use a per-session calibration clamped to 0.5 to 2.0. When turns leave the model's view without a summary covering them, the run first **compacts** them with the agent's own model (no tools, at most 1,024 output tokens, temperature 0.2, summary at most 8 KiB, a 2-minute deadline) unless `autoCompact` is `false`; `POST .../compact` does it on demand. A failure leaves `compactionError` on the session and the run continues with trimmed context.

## The Run Ledger

Every message to an agent becomes a **run** in a durable ledger (`runs/ledger.rs`).

| Aspect | Values |
|--------|--------|
| Status | `queued`, `running`, `awaiting_approval`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted` |
| Source | `web`, `api`, `telegram`, `discord`, `schedule`, `job`, `delegation`, `peer` |
| Retention | Finished runs kept 24 hours, at most 50 per agent in the ledger, then read from the history store |
| Limits | Input text 32 KiB, 10 attachments, 50 recorded steps, 50 recorded tool starts, 50 action receipts |

`POST /api/agents/{id}/sessions/{sid}/runs` (with an `Idempotency-Key`) answers `202` with a `queued` run that starts once the session's earlier messages finish and an agent slot and a global permit are free. At most 8 messages may wait per agent (`MAX_QUEUED_RUNS_PER_AGENT`); the ninth gets `429`. Runs in the same room always execute in order; different rooms of one agent run concurrently up to `ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_RUNS_PER_AGENT`. Helpers always run one task at a time.

A run's tool results are mirrored as **action receipts** (`actionReceipts` on run reads): intent is saved before a handler dispatches and the outcome before the result is returned, so after a crash a `started` receipt means "outcome unknown". Previews are capped at 2,048 bytes. Nothing is replayed automatically.

### Isolation

Concurrent rooms of one agent run on isolated copies of the runtime and merge back what each run added (`RuntimeRunDelta`, see [AgentRuntime](/architecture/rust-core/anima-core/agent-runtime/#concurrent-rooms)); a rejected or unsaveable result is rolled back with `run.failed` (`commit_rejected`, `commit_failed` or `agent_deleted`).

## Steer and Stop

**Steer.** `POST .../runs` with `"mode": "steer"` while the session has a running run adds the message to that run's `SteeringInbox`. The run reads it before its next model call (`run.steered`). A steer the run never reads becomes a queued message after the run ends, or an `interrupted` run (`queue_full_before_start`) if 8 are already waiting. After a restart each unread steer comes back as `interrupted` (`restart_before_start`). A retried key answers `200` with the run it joined.

**Stop.** `POST /api/agents/{id}/runs/{run_id}/stop` answers `202`. A queued run is cancelled immediately. A running run records `stop.requestedAtMs` *before* the cancel signal is sent, then ends `cancelled` at its next checkpoint: before the next model call, while streaming (the request is dropped), or before the next tool batch. Tools already running finish except `bash`, whose direct child is killed; background processes keep running. Streamed text stays as a message marked `stopped`, never-run tool calls get `Cancelled before running (stopped by owner)`, helpers and delegations started by the run are stopped too, and unread steers become `interrupted` runs (`stopped_before_start`). A job attempt stopped this way moves the job to `needs_review`; a stopped schedule fire records `stopped` and the schedule stays enabled.

## Live Events

`GET /api/agents/{id}/events` is one SSE stream per agent covering the agent, its helpers and delegated sessions (`live/`). The first event is `stream.snapshot` (active runs, their current step text up to 64 KiB and tool cards, up to 50). Then:

| Group | Events |
|-------|--------|
| Sessions | `session.created`, `session.updated`, `session.deleted` |
| Runs | `run.queued`, `run.started`, `run.awaiting_approval`, `run.progress` (for example `phase: "compacting"`), `run.steered`, `run.completed`, `run.failed`, `run.cancelled`, `run.interrupted` |
| Output | `step.delta` (flushed at least every 50 ms or 512 bytes), `message.created`, `tool.started`, `tool.finished`, `model.fallback` |
| Approvals | `approval.requested`, `approval.resolved` |
| Other | `skill.updated`, `automation.updated` |

Every event has `type`, `agentId`, optional `sessionId` / `runId`, a per-stream `seq` (also the SSE `id`) and `at`. A stream that falls behind gets `stream.resync` with `missed`; there is no replay, so a reconnect starts from a new snapshot (`Last-Event-ID` is ignored). Keep-alive comments every 15 seconds; at most 16 open streams per agent (`429`). Browsers allow about 6 connections per origin over HTTP/1.1, so many open console tabs can starve other requests through the dev proxy.

## Approvals

Every native tool has a risk class (`approvals/policy.rs`):

| Class | Tools (examples) |
|-------|------------------|
| read | `read_file`, `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`, `read_document`, `memory_search`, `recent_memories`, `bg_list`, `bg_output`, `bg_wait`, `app_read`, `acp_read`, `load_skill`, `list_automations`, `drive_search`, `drive_read`, `calendar_list_events`, `mail_list_messages`, `search_conversations` |
| write | `write_file`, `edit_file`, `multi_edit`, `todo_write`, `memory_add`, `core_memory`, `memory_update`, `memory_remove`, `memory_consolidate`, `propose_skill`, `create_automation`, `update_automation`, `delete_automation`, `mail_create_draft`, `calendar_*` writes, `acp_edit` |
| exec | `bash`, `execute_code`, `bg_start`, `bg_stop`, `browser_*`, `app_start`, `app_send`, `app_stop`, `acp_start`, `acp_prompt`, `acp_cancel`, `acp_stop`, `acp_execute`, `acp_other`; **any tool the table does not name** |
| network | `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `exa_search`, `acp_fetch` |
| delegate | `delegate_to_agent`, `spawn_helper`, `spawn_helper_async`, `steer_helper`, `stop_helper`, `send_message`, `broadcast_message`, `trigger_automation` |

Each agent has a policy (`write`, `exec`, `network`, `delegate`, each `allow`, `ask` or `deny`), rules and per-session allowances. Read-class tools never ask. The **autonomy** modes (`approvals/autonomy.rs`) are presets: **Free** (all four classes `allow`), **Strict** (`write`, `exec` and `delegate` ask; `network` allowed) and **Custom** (the owner's own class choices, and the mode of every agent saved before autonomy existed). In every mode a floor stays: destructive commands are blocked, the owner's deny patterns are blocked (at most 50, 200 characters each), and commands that are hard to undo still ask unless an owner rule covers them.

Judging order (`evaluate` and `evaluate_with_floor`): for shell commands the autonomy floor comes first (a blocked command is denied; a hard-to-undo one asks unless a rule or allowance covers it, and still denies if the class is `deny`). Then a class set to `deny` denies, a matching rule or session allowance allows, a class set to `ask` asks, and everything else is allowed. Plans ask even where their class is allowed, unless covered (in Free mode they follow their class). Matchers: `command_prefix` (shell commands; any command containing a chaining, substitution or redirect operator never matches a prefix rule, and wrapper commands such as `sh`, `env`, `sudo`, `python` are not suggested as prefixes), `path_glob` (writes), `domain` (fetches) and `any`. A rule or allowance for a read-class tool is refused.

A call that needs the owner waits up to 30 minutes (15 for a Telegram-started run) with its run `awaiting_approval`. Decisions (`allow_once`, `allow_session`, `allow_always`, `deny`) are saved before the call proceeds; at most 100 rules per agent and 50 allowances per session; a stale `revision` returns `409`. Helpers never wait: a call that would ask is denied. A restart expires every pending approval. Decided approvals move to the history store and stay readable for 30 days. A run, job or Telegram message that calls an asking tool holds its lane while it waits.

Agent-file writes (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.anima.md` and similar instruction files) need an exact owner decision even under reusable allow rules; see the README section "Standard Markdown agent files".

## Jobs and Goals

A **job** is a durable unit of delegated work (`jobs.rs`): `title`, `prompt`, a `requestKey` (idempotent create), status (`awaiting_approval`, `queued`, `running`, `pending_delegations`, `completed`, `failed`, `needs_review`, `cancelled`, `stopped` for an attempt), up to 3 attempts by default, optional required approval, and owner review of outputs (`accepted` or `changes_requested`). Up to 200 jobs are kept and 8 run at once. A **goal** groups jobs under an attempt budget (`active`, `paused`, `completed`) and reports consumed, reserved and remaining attempts and accepted outputs. Routes: `/api/agents/{id}/jobs...` (create, approve, cancel, retry, review) and `/api/goals...`. A job attempt that was uncertain when the daemon stopped goes to `needs_review`; retrying it needs `acknowledgeUncertain`.

## Automations

Prompts the daemon sends an agent on a trigger (`schedules.rs`, `schedules/`): `interval { intervalMs }`, `daily { hour, minute, timeZone }`, `cron { expression, timeZone }` (five fields, plus `@hourly`, `@daily` and friends), or `once { atMs }`. Times are wall clock in the IANA `timeZone`; `activeHours { start, end, days, timeZone }` keeps fires inside a window. Limits: 20 automations per agent, prompts up to 32 KiB, 8 scheduled jobs running at once, agent-created ones at least 5 minutes apart over their next 10 fires. Each occurrence is persisted before it runs and its outcome (`silent`, `spoke`, `failed`, `stopped`) is kept as a fire record mirrored to the history store. A claimed occurrence with no terminal outcome at startup disables that schedule (`schedule_run_interrupted`) for owner review. A check-in reply of exactly `CHECKIN_OK` means "nothing to say". `POST /api/schedules/preview` computes the next fire times so browsers never compute schedules.

This is separate from the `anima-schedule` crate; see [anima-schedule](/architecture/rust-core/anima-schedule/).

## Skills and Learning

Skills are `<workspace>/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` files pinned to the SHA-256 the owner approved; an edited file reads `changed` and is never loaded until re-approved. Agents propose skills as drafts; in Free mode approved changes are recorded in a ledger and can be reverted. Task reviews (2 per agent per day) and [conversation reviews](/architecture/rust-core/anima-memory/daemon-memory/#conversation-reviews) can propose memory edits and skill drafts. Routes: `/api/skills...`, `/api/skill-drafts...`, `/api/skill-ledger`, `/api/agents/{id}/learning-*`.

## Shutdown and Restart

See [Rust Daemon](/hosts/rust-daemon/#graceful-shutdown). After a restart: queued runs end `interrupted` (`restart_before_start`), runs that were going end `interrupted` (`restart_during_run`), pending approvals expire and the daemon never resumes a model call mid-turn. Draining (`POST /api/system/drain`) refuses new chat messages, legacy runs, peer messages, connector sends, swarm runs, jobs and goals with `503` while accepted runs finish; due automations and queued jobs stay due.
The Postgres container profile for the Rust daemon and the one-owner VPS package

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

<Aside type="caution" title="Read this before binding to 0.0.0.0">
  Owner-only routes (sessions, runs, approvals, connectors, usage, logs, memory edits, the workspace file browser and the rest of the console's API) require a **loopback bind** and a loopback `Host`, and reject forwarding headers. A daemon bound to `0.0.0.0` behind a proxy answers those routes with `403 local owner authorization required`. The profile below serves the agent, swarm, memory, health and readiness APIs; for the full console behind TLS use the VPS package, which keeps the daemon on loopback.
</Aside>

<Aside type="caution" title="Single replica">
  Run one daemon. Vector indexes are process-local and rebuilt from the memory snapshot on startup, and run state, workers and connector pollers live in one process.
</Aside>

## Container Profile (Postgres)

`hosts/rust-daemon/Dockerfile` builds from the repository root:

```bash
docker build -f hosts/rust-daemon/Dockerfile -t anima-daemon:staging .
```

It is a two-stage build (Chainguard Rust builder running `cargo build --release --locked -p anima-daemon`, Wolfi runtime with `ca-certificates`, `libgomp` and `libstdc++`), runs as a non-root user (`uid 10001`), sets `ANIMAOS_RS_HOST=0.0.0.0` and `ANIMAOS_RS_PORT=8080`, exposes 8080 and starts `/usr/local/bin/anima-daemon`.

`hosts/rust-daemon/.env.staging.example` is the env profile. Translate it into your platform's secret settings; do not commit real values.

### Durability

With Postgres as the source of truth:

- The control plane (agents, swarms, sessions, runs, settings, connector records) and the memory snapshot are `host_snapshots` rows (`control_plane`, `memory`).
- Step logs and explicit retry-key reuse use `step_log`.
- History uses the `history_*` tables (Postgres 12 or newer).
- Leave `ANIMAOS_RS_CONTROL_PLANE_FILE`, `ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_FILE` and `ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_SQLITE_FILE` unset unless those paths are on a persistent disk.
- Vectors stay in process. If cold-start rebuilds get expensive and you have a persistent volume, set `ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_SQLITE_FILE`.
- Credentials (bot tokens, OAuth tokens, ChatGPT login) use the OS credential store, which a bare container does not provide. The VPS package supplies a keyring; the plain image above does not include one, so features that must store secrets (connectors, ChatGPT sign-in) cannot rely on it.

## Required Environment

```bash
ANIMAOS_RS_HOST=0.0.0.0
ANIMAOS_RS_PORT=8080
ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE=postgres
DATABASE_URL=postgres://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:5432/anima_staging
ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS=local
RUST_LOG=info,tower_http=info
```

Set at least one provider key (for example `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`). The example file also sets `ANIMAOS_RS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS=60`, `ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES=262144`, `ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS=8` and `ANIMAOS_RS_MAX_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES=4`. Set `ANIMAOS_RS_API_KEY` for anything reachable beyond the host: without it the daemon trusts the network.

<Aside type="note">
  The daemon runs embedded migrations at startup. If `ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE=postgres` is set and Postgres is unavailable or a migration fails, startup fails; there is no silent fallback to memory mode.
</Aside>

## Vector Strategy

The default embedding mode is `fastembed`, an in-process ONNX model that downloads on first use and needs model cache space (`ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_CACHE_DIR`). The staging example pins `local` (hashed vectors, no download). The other options push embedding work to an endpoint: `ollama`, `openai`, `openai-compatible`. See [Memory in the Daemon](/architecture/rust-core/anima-memory/daemon-memory/#embeddings).

## Checklist

<Steps>

1. Provision a managed Postgres database (12 or newer).

2. Set `ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE=postgres` and `DATABASE_URL`.

3. Leave file-based store variables unset unless the platform provides a persistent disk.

4. Start one replica from the image built above.

5. Verify liveness and readiness:

   ```bash
   curl https://staging.example.com/health
   curl https://staging.example.com/ready
   ```

6. Confirm `/ready` reports `controlPlaneDurability: "postgres"` and `database: "configured"`.

</Steps>

## What This Does Not Claim

Postgres staging restores registered agents, swarms, latest snapshots, swarm message history, sessions, the run ledger and memory snapshots, and lets a retried request reuse completed tool steps. It does not resume a model call from the middle after a restart: work that was running is restored as failed or interrupted so callers retry on purpose.

## One-Owner VPS Package

`deploy/vps/` builds the web console and the daemon and puts Caddy in front: HTTPS, one HTTP Basic owner login, and a gateway that checks Origin and Fetch Metadata and translates the authenticated owner into the daemon's internal API key and admin token. The daemon shares the gateway's network namespace and listens only on `127.0.0.1:8080`; only ports 80 and 443 are published. It is intended for one trusted owner, one daemon and one VPS; it is not multi-user and not a sandbox for hostile agent code.

Key points (`deploy/vps/README.md` is the full procedure):

- The Compose project is `anima-companion`. The daemon runs with `ANIMAOS_RS_PERSISTENCE_MODE=memory` plus explicit files under `/state` (`control-plane.json`, `memory.sqlite`, `history.sqlite`), `ANIMAOS_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/workspace` and `ANIMAOS_RS_MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS=local`.
- Five named volumes (`daemon_state`, `workspace`, `daemon_home`, `caddy_data`, `caddy_config`) plus the protected `.env` and the image ids form one backup generation; back up with the daemon stopped and restore all of them together.
- Secrets (`ANIMA_INTERNAL_API_KEY`, `ANIMA_LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN`, `ANIMA_KEYRING_PASSWORD`) are mandatory with no defaults. The image runs a private D-Bus session and GNOME Secret Service, unlocks the persisted login keyring at startup and probes a write, read and delete before the daemon starts; a wrong password fails startup instead of using transient credentials. Never replace `ANIMA_KEYRING_PASSWORD` to troubleshoot an existing vault.
- `ANIMA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://<domain>` sets the OAuth callback origin for Google and Microsoft apps.
- Verification is by contract tests (`deploy/vps/contracts.test.ts`, the `deployment-contracts` Nx target of `web-e2e`) and manual acceptance (public TLS, real providers, reboot, off-site restore); the package is not verified by starting containers in CI.
